subject.title: sessions_send blocked by visibility guard even when a2a policy allows cross-agent messaging

question: Should cross-agent `sessions_send` be allowed under `tools.sessions.visibility="tree"` when `tools.agentToAgent` explicitly allows the requester and target, or should this wait for a broader granular visibility policy?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix intentionally changes the boundary between message injection and transcript/session visibility, which automation should not decide without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Approve bounded send-only A2A
options.body: Allow cross-agent `send` to use A2A policy as the authority while requiring regression proof that list, history, status, and sandbox spawned scopes stay restricted.

options.title: Fold into granular visibility
options.body: Keep this issue open but route implementation through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48785 so one policy model owns per-capability visibility.

options.title: Keep current fail-closed behavior
options.body: Continue requiring `visibility="all"` for cross-agent sends and document the tradeoff as intentional for now.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded send-only A2A
recommendation.body: Allow cross-agent `send` to use A2A policy as the authority while requiring regression proof that list, history, status, and sandbox spawned scopes stay restricted.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to this handle for the sandbox visibility and session access helper architecture, and the choice is an owner-boundary/security policy decision on that surface.
